LESSON: CROP PROTECTION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Crop Production
Topic 1.6: Crop Protection
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Crop Protection, part of Crop Production in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How do weeds affect crop production? 2. Why is weed control done in crop production?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Crop Protection together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Responsibility: learner develops a sense of obligation when carrying out weed control in a crop field.

● Respect: learner shows regards for others when discussing making presentations on pros and cons of weeds to a

farming household.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental Conservation: learners discusses the effects of irresponsible chemical weed control on the

environment and how this can be minimised.

● Guidance Services: Learner decides on materials to use when making herbarium and methods to apply in controlling

weeds.

Suggested Learning Resources:

● Photographs of weeds in appropriate colour contrast

● Various types of weeds

● Weeds herbarium

● Local environment

● Digital devices with assistive technology

● Blotting paper or newspaper

● Plant press or two rigid boards made from wood or metal
